articleBody: Seismic retrofitting and foundation repair are related but not identical services, and Los Angeles homeowners often need both evaluated together. FEMA guidance on earthquake safety explains that strengthening a house against seismic loads commonly involves bolting the framing to the foundation, adding shear resistance, and addressing weak connections in crawlspace or cripple-wall conditions. If the foundation itself is damaged, settlement, cracking, or deterioration may have to be repaired before or during the retrofit. This distinction matters because a contractor who only installs retrofit hardware may miss underlying foundation defects, while a contractor focused only on foundation repair may not address lateral load resistance. Los Angeles County sits in a high seismic risk region, so buyers should ask whether the contractor coordinates structural assessment, engineering, and permit documentation. In many cases, the work requires stamped plans or engineering calculations, especially when the house has significant irregularities, previous additions, or soft-story conditions. Homeowners should also confirm whether the proposal includes access improvements, crawlspace clearance, sill-plate replacement if needed, and inspection of utilities that may need temporary disconnection. The best practice is to obtain an inspection that distinguishes cosmetic cracking from structural movement and then match the remedy to the actual condition. Contractors who can explain the difference between retrofit objectives and foundation stabilization usually provide better scope control and fewer surprises during construction.
